name: Documents, templates and tools together
description: Explanation, fill-in templates, an ordered set of steps and the author's skill, read by people and agents, with the esoi tools beside them: the records are checked on every change, alternatives are measured, and the implementation the metric ranks best is the one selected. The documents carry what a person must decide; the tools carry what can be checked.
advantages: Records are checked rather than trusted, so humans need only review metrics (and can still add value to implementations); the documents still work for anyone who never installs the tools. Selected because: a declared decision pending measurement: with the tools the records are checked and the best implementation is selected by metric (principle 4), where documents only leave both to the reader
disadvantages: The tools are Python and cost upkeep; a reader who skips the documents still builds records the tools cannot judge.

name: Documents only, applied by hand
description: The same explanation, templates and steps, with records kept as documents, a sheet or a board by a person or an agent, and metrics read from whatever notes someone keeps. Nothing is installed.
advantages: Needs no code or install, works in any place records can be written, and is the quickest start (the one-hour guide).
disadvantages: Nothing checks the records, links drift unnoticed, and nothing selects the best implementation, so reviewers fall back to reading implementations.

name: Records in the esoi folder
description: Every record of the top intent in one CSV per type under the project's `esoi/` folder, edited by hand and read by the check, the tracker and the selection; a sub-intent is a folder of its own inside it.
advantages: Versioned with the code it describes, diffable, readable by any tool and any AI, public with the repository; the whole network is in one place. The layout before records beside the code. Not selected: it passes none of the 53 solutions measured, because the spec of each is far from its code and no code folder has a README; it passes the clicks, duplication and determinism checks. It stays an arm for a repository whose build or framework fixes its folder structure.
disadvantages: The spec of a solution is far from its code, so the reader moves between two trees; a code folder carries no page of its own; long text is awkward in CSV, and concurrent edits by several agents can collide in one file.

name: Records beside the code
description: Each solution's records live once, in the folder that holds its code (the lowest folder that holds all of its implementations), next to that code; the folders are named in `[records] beside_code` in esoi.toml, the library reads them as part of the same tree, and each folder gets a generated README. The top intent stays in `esoi/` with its intent.csv; a sub-intent is a folder with its own intent.csv beside its code. `esoi records place` moves the records there.
advantages: A solution's spec and code are in the same folder or one link apart; every code folder that holds an implementation has a page that says what it is; nothing is copied or gathered, so no record is kept twice; folders of folders show the intent hierarchy as the code is organized. Selected because: it passes 47 of the 53 solutions measured (this repository and the first adopting repository) on the navigable-records checks where the esoi folder passes none, a significant lead (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=1.4e-14); the 6 it fails have code in folders more than one link from the lowest folder that may hold their records.
disadvantages: Cross-cutting problems and ideals live with the lowest folder that holds all of their solutions, so the whole network is read through the top README and the generated pages rather than one file; the code folders carry data files and a README that are not code.

name: Sheet as source
description: The Google Sheet holds the records and the repository pulls a copy.
advantages: The easiest place for a person to write and refine.
disadvantages: Not versioned with the code, needs credentials, and a public repository cannot depend on a private sheet.

name: Template parser
description: A script reads the intent template's sections and fields from `SKILL.md` and writes the committed field list.
advantages: The author's words are the only definition, and a refinement needs no schema edit. Selected because: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
disadvantages: Depends on the template keeping a parseable shape; wording changes can rename fields.

name: Hand-kept field list
description: Someone copies the template's fields into a schema when the template changes.
advantages: No parser to maintain.
disadvantages: Drifts exactly as the problem describes.

name: Component rows
description: `components.csv` lists each component's layer, path globs, role and solutions; the check matches every file to exactly one row.
advantages: Small, explicit, checked on every change. Selected because: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
disadvantages: Globs need upkeep as files move.

name: Declarations in code
description: Each implementation is declared where its code is (`@implementation`, or `register` for an object that cannot carry a decorator), and the records list the same implementations with the path of their module, so there is no second list to keep. A call runs the implementation one cascade chooses (per call, context, environment, deployment, then the solution's selected cell in the records), importing it lazily. A selection table written by hand still works underneath. The esoi-runtime sub-intent elaborates it for other people's running code.
advantages: No logic at call sites and no hand-kept table, optional dependencies load only when chosen, typos fail with the choices, and a switch is data in the layer that should decide it. Selected because: it is the only arm built, and the cases of Selection at Run Time pin the behaviour a rival must keep.
disadvantages: Declaring needs the esoi package at run time, and the module of an implementation must be named in its record so it can be imported when chosen.

name: Entry-point plugins
description: Implementations register through Python package entry points.
advantages: Third parties add implementations without touching the library.
disadvantages: Discovery depends on installation state, and the default is harder to see.

name: Component harness
description: One folder per solution with cases, a scorer and implementation files that drive live code; `esoi run --record` appends provenance-stamped rows to `results.csv`.
advantages: Measures shipped code, versioned with it, no outside service. Selected because: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
disadvantages: Built and maintained by us; less tooling than dedicated eval platforms.

name: External eval platform
description: promptfoo, LangSmith or a similar tool runs the cases and stores results.
advantages: Mature reporting and comparison views.
disadvantages: Results outside the repository, harder to tie to the selection and the check, often tests prompts apart from the shipped code.

name: Margin leaderboard
description: Compares the latest result of each implementation on the same case hash, calls a win only beyond a pass-rate margin or spend tolerance, and labels ties, losses, unmeasured and comparison-only arms.
advantages: Honest about noise; one ranking reused by the check. Selected because: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
disadvantages: Fixed margins are a rough stand-in for proper confidence intervals.

name: Broken baselines
description: Each solution with a single implementation keeps naive implementations in its `broken/` folder, and one test proves each fails the cases.
advantages: Cheap proof that the cases mean something. Selected because: it is the only arm built, and one test proves each naive implementation fails its cases.
disadvantages: Proves only against the naive versions someone thought to write.

name: Rule script
description: `esoi check` runs every registered rule group over the tree, registry and results, with strict mode, disabled ids, plugins and waivers.
advantages: One runner for every rule, fast, runs before commit and in tests; a plugin adds a rule without touching it. Selected because: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
disadvantages: A custom tool to maintain.

name: Numbered rule modules
description: Rules written as Python functions grouped by what they check, each with an id and a one-line statement, shipped with the library and extended by plugins.
advantages: Enforced in code and named by id and path; a repository adds its own by plugin. Selected because: the only built implementation; prose rules are the baseline the problem describes, and its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
disadvantages: The reason for a rule is not recorded beside it, and the ids give no hint of what they check.

name: Rules in prose
description: The rules written in the standard document and followed by whoever read it, with code review as the check.
advantages: Costs nothing to write or change.
disadvantages: Followed by whoever read them and broken by the next agent.

name: Tracker and sheet
description: `esoi tracker build` generates the tracker tables from the registry and results; `esoi sheet-sync` merges them two-way with the Google Sheet by record id, keeping reviewer columns.
advantages: The reviewer works in a sheet while the repository stays the source. Selected because: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
disadvantages: Only review columns flow back, so other edits in the sheet are overwritten.

name: Consumer command
description: `esoi consumer check` reads the consumer's own registry, requirements and results, and the library's cases score the consumer's stores through `--impl module:build`.
advantages: One implementation of the checks for every consumer; private cases stay private. Selected because: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
disadvantages: The consumer must keep its registry in the library's shape.

name: Standard document
description: `docs/explanation/intent-types.md` gives the shape of a solution and the other four record types, and `docs/how-to/apply-with-tools.md` the steps to adopt them; `esoi rules` lists what is checked.
advantages: Two short documents to read first. Selected because: it is the only arm built.
disadvantages: Prose can drift from the rules unless updated with them.

name: Written weighing rule
description: Before adding a sub-intent, rule or record, weigh its build and upkeep cost against what comparing alternatives and defining it clearly would gain, counted to the next highest priority milestone (docs/explanation/when-to-create-a-sub-intent.md), and weigh it again at each milestone.
advantages: Costs nothing to adopt, works without code, and applies to any project. Selected because: it is the only arm built; weighing measured cost against catches needs a log of what each rule catches.
disadvantages: Depends on people applying it; nothing measures the structure's cost automatically.

name: Measured cost and catches
description: A tool records the time the check adds and which rules, records and checks caught a real violation, and proposes removing those that catch nothing over a period.
advantages: Makes the cost visible and pruning evidence-based.
disadvantages: Needs tooling and a history of catches; not every project merits it.

name: On a decision
description: Run a metric when a choice depends on its result: a new alternative, a selection change or a suspected regression.
advantages: Spends only where a choice depends on the result, and a stale result still informs. Selected because: Joshua's decision of 2026-11-04 that a changed file only informs and a metric is re-run when a decision depends on it, since code changes many times a day.
disadvantages: Someone has to notice that a decision is coming.

name: On every change
description: Run a metric whenever the measured code or its cases change.
advantages: Results are always current; nothing is found late.
disadvantages: Unaffordable for a paid or slow metric.

name: On a schedule
description: Run a metric at a fixed interval whatever changed.
advantages: Catches drift in the world without anyone noticing it.
disadvantages: Runs that change nothing; a stale result can still be used between runs.

name: On drift
description: Run a metric when a cheap probe or an announcement says the world moved.
advantages: Re-measures exactly when it matters.
disadvantages: Needs a probe that is itself maintained.

name: Generated public copy
description: A command copies the listed files from the private folder, removes marked private passages, applies the few listed substitutions, and a second command checks freshness and leaks.
advantages: One source of truth; drift and leaks are found by a check, not by memory. Selected because: the only implementation built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep
disadvantages: The source must mark its private passages, and the private term list lives outside the repository so only the author can run the full check.

name: Hand-copied folder
description: Someone copies the public files by hand and edits out what is private.
advantages: No tooling.
disadvantages: Drifts at the first edit and nothing catches a missed private fragment.

name: Publish the private folder
description: Publish the whole folder as it is.
advantages: No copy to maintain.
disadvantages: Publishes people, paths and internal process; not acceptable.

name: Skill as standing instructions
description: The author's skill is loaded as the system text of every session, so the agent reads the principles before any task and ends its work with a short summary of how it applied them.
advantages: The principles are always in context, no loading decision can go wrong, and one file is the source of truth. Selected because: a declared decision pending measurement: standing instructions are how the author's skill is meant to be used, and the choice stands until a measured arm beats it.
disadvantages: Costs the skill's tokens on every task, including tasks it does not fit, and can push an agent to add structure where none is wanted unless the restraint cases are met.

name: Skill on request
description: The agent sees only the skill's name and description and loads the full text when it judges that the task is about design, reuse or how it should behave; the measurement includes that loading decision.
advantages: Costs tokens only when used and keeps other tasks uncluttered.
disadvantages: Two to three model calls per measured case, and it depends on the agent recognising when the principles apply: a missed load means no principles at all.

name: No skill
description: The agent works from its general training and the person's corrections in conversation; measured with the same model and a plain assistant instruction, so what the skill adds is a number.
advantages: Costs nothing and has nothing to maintain.
disadvantages: Corrections are forgotten between sessions, and the behaviour cannot be improved by a measure.

name: Perspective review
description: After drafting, the agent asks named perspectives, each an implementation of what good looks like, to review the draft against the principles, and revises it.
advantages: Applies principle 7 directly: alternative perspectives are kept and none is assumed best.
disadvantages: Several more calls per task, and not built or measured yet.

name: The ESOI steps
description: Twenty-three ordered steps in five parts, from purpose to selection by metric, with human steps marked, a map of where to loop back, and a section applying the steps to themselves.
advantages: Carries out every principle, decides best before building, checks the metric before trusting it, and ships with the skill to every agent and reader. Selected because: a declared decision pending measurement: the steps are the only implementation that carries out every principle, and the choice stands until a recorded trial shows another does better.
disadvantages: Longer than a newcomer may want for a small task, so it relies on sizing each step to the work.

name: Project Documentation board checklist
description: The eighteen-item 2020 Trello checklist the steps grew from: purpose, brainstorm, audience, problems, knowledge, ideals, coverage, difficulties, definitions, implementations, carrying out, better alternatives, keep improving.
advantages: Short, proven on several boards, and needs only Trello.
disadvantages: Leaves out the split test, interfaces, metric checks and cost, perspectives, a baseline, recorded selection and retirement.

name: One-hour first pass
description: The guide for applying ESOI by hand in about an hour (docs/how-to/apply-by-hand.md): an overall network, one detailed solution, a small metric, a recorded choice, then habits.
advantages: Fast start that already ends in a measured choice.
disadvantages: Covers early steps only briefly and skips the review from other perspectives.

name: No stated order
description: The record types and principles alone, applied in whatever order the person chooses.
advantages: Nothing to learn or maintain.
disadvantages: It leaves the problem this solution exists to address as it is.

name: Documentation folder
description: Hand-written explanation and guides beside templates generated from the skill.
advantages: Needs no code and stays in step with the skill. Selected because: it is the only arm built.
disadvantages: Prose can drift unless regenerated and reviewed.

name: Model judge on the rubric
description: A model grades each reply against the case's expected behaviour and failure mode in words, never seeing the patterns or the recorded replies, with the patterns as a prefilter.
advantages: Credits a reply that acts well in other words and catches vocabulary without behaviour. Selected because: a declared decision pending measurement: it is the only arm that can credit a reply that acts well in other words, and it is used only with its agreement shown.
disadvantages: Costs a call per reply, may favour its own phrasing, and is only as good as its agreement with people.

name: Regex checks only
description: Patterns that every reply must match and that none may match.
advantages: Free, instant, deterministic and easy to review, and it makes the circularity of the labels visible.
disadvantages: Passes keyword stuffing, fails a correct reply in other words, and agrees with its author's labels by construction, so its agreement shows that circularity rather than calibration.

name: Human review of every reply
description: A person reads and marks every reply.
advantages: The authority on what counts, so it needs no calibration.
disadvantages: Does not scale and uses the scarcest time. It is the source of the labels that calibrate the other judges, not a replacement for them.

name: Declarations read from the code, rows synced
description: The code declares a solution and its alternatives with decorators. The declarations are read without importing the code, what the records lack is reported (rule S30), and the missing rows are written with only what the code knows. One command writes the records, a code skeleton and an evaluation folder together for a new solution.
advantages: One place to declare; the records cannot silently lack an alternative; the measured code is never imported to read it. Selected because: the only one built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep, and the hand-kept baseline fails them
disadvantages: Python only, and the scan reads the decorators by name, so an unusual alias of them is missed; the text only a person can write is still theirs to write.

name: Records kept by hand
description: A person adds the alternative to the code and writes its records separately; a check, if there is one, only reports the drift.
advantages: No dependency on declarations; works in any language.
disadvantages: A second copy held in step by upkeep, skipped under deadline, and the drift is found late.

name: Record tables only
description: A page is written into every intent folder from its records: what the intent is, how its solutions fit together in one paragraph, then its problems, ideals, solutions, implementations and metrics by id, in file order. The check reports a page that differs from what the records generate.
advantages: Complete and cannot disagree with the records; one command regenerates it. Not selected: it passes none of the 4 intent folders on the glance checks, because the record comes before anything that says what the intent is.
disadvantages: A reader meets the whole record before learning what the intent is; it shows no diagram, no entry calls and no links to sub-intents, the parent or the repository.

name: At a glance, full record below
description: The page opens with the name, vision statement and opportunities, the paragraph on how the solutions fit, the solution diagram inline, a table of each solution's one-line entry call and selected implementation, problems and ideals in a line each, metrics with their current leader and links to the sub-intents, the parent intent and the repository's top README. A divider follows, and below it the full record tables.
advantages: A reader learns what the intent is, how it fits and where to go next on the first screen; the diagram and the entry calls come from the records and the code, so nothing is hand-kept. Selected because: it passes all 4 intent folders on the glance checks where the record tables alone and the compact page pass none (a best guess on 4 folders, not yet significant).
disadvantages: Longer than the record tables alone, because the summary repeats ids; a long coherence paragraph pushes the diagram down the page.

name: Compact page of links
description: The page holds the name, the vision statement and links: to each sub-intent, the parent intent, the repository's top README and each record file with its row count.
advantages: Short to read and to review; nothing in it can go stale except the links. Not selected: it passes none of the 4 intent folders, because it shows no coherence paragraph, diagram or solution rows.
disadvantages: The reader must open other files to learn how the solutions fit or what to call.

name: README written by hand
description: A person writes a summary of the intent beside the records.
advantages: Can explain what the records do not.
disadvantages: Repeats the records, so it drifts from them, and nothing notices.

name: Promotion on the leaderboard's verdict
description: Where a rival beats the selected implementation on the same cases beyond the noise, the solution's selected cell and the metric's command are switched and the evidence is written beside them, when the solution's promotion cell says automatic; otherwise the same edits are printed as a proposal.
advantages: Reuses the ranking the check already trusts; refuses unverified, incomparable and stale results; leaves the choice to a person where the policy asks. Selected because: the only one built; its cases pin the behaviour any rival must keep, and never promoting fails them
disadvantages: Rests on the leaderboard's fixed margins; knows only the metric's own cases, not whether the rival is acceptable in other ways.

name: A person edits the records
description: A person reads the board, then edits the selected cell, the metric command and the reason by hand.
advantages: A person sees every switch.
disadvantages: A chore that is postponed, and the evidence for the switch is often not written down.

name: Field-weighted TF-IDF over the index
description: Each entry's terms carry the weight of the heaviest field they appeared in (id and name 3, summary 2, body 1); a query term scores that weight times its inverse document frequency, taken from the index itself; hits can pull in linked records.
advantages: Rare terms count more and a word in a record's name counts more than one in its body; deterministic; the index carries its own statistics, so a consumer needs no corpus pass. Selected because: the metric: it must rank the expected records higher than plain term overlap on the same cases
disadvantages: Lexical only: a request that shares no word with a record's text finds nothing, which is why a consumer adds semantic search.

name: Plain term overlap
description: Count the terms a request shares with a record, every term and field worth the same.
advantages: The simplest possible baseline; shows what weighting buys.
disadvantages: Common words in a long record outweigh the rare word that identifies it.

name: Library modules
description: The spec_slice, metric_meter, metric_results and iteration modules wired for one piece of work: a slice of the specification, meters that read the metric, a ledger of rows and MetricIteration around them.
advantages: A program reads the values, so the record does not depend on a model or on the worker's word; every setting is an argument and nothing is read from the environment; the slice source, the meters and the ledger can each be replaced alone.
disadvantages: A metric that has no current recorded row and no offline arm gets no reading after the work, and a reading that exceeds its budget is dropped, so some work is recorded with only one of the two values.

name: Lexical vector gated
description: Lexical plus vector candidates, fused, then the gate: a clear case and an empty case are answered with no judge call, any other costs one call over the best ``gate.pool`` candidates. ``strategy`` ``judge-all`` and ``lexical`` run the other two stagings with the same arguments.
advantages: A clear or empty case costs no judge call and every other costs one; the judge is kept for requests that need it; with no judge the fused candidates are the answer.
disadvantages: The gate thresholds were tuned for one product's records and embedding model and need measuring on another's.

name: Lexical only
description: The baseline: the lexical top three, no vector search and no judge. Free and instant; shows what the rest adds.
advantages: Free, instant and deterministic; shows what the vector search and judge add.
disadvantages: Finds nothing when the request shares no word with a record.

name: Letter grades by weighted evidence
description: Grades each candidate and dimension from the evidence rows by the visible weights table: a letter from A to D, the flags raised, and the one run of the repository's own that would settle it.
advantages: No model call and no cost; each weight has its reason and can be replaced with Params; a conflict with the repository's own results is reported, not hidden.
disadvantages: It grades only evidence a person has already collected, and the weights are judgments, so another table can grade the same rows differently.

name: Repo wide
description: Any tracked file of the repository's code paths or evaluation folder that changed since the row's commit makes every row stale.
advantages: Safe: it never keeps a result whose measured code changed; needs no ownership map.
disadvantages: Every commit stales every component, so metrics are re-run for components whose measured code did not change.

name: Component paths
description: Only the files the arm's solution and implementation own in the ownership map (path globs mapped to solutions, the implementation records' files, a records folder that holds the solution's code alone, the component's evaluation folder and the shared fixtures) make the row stale; an unowned file counts for every arm and a component with no ownership entry keeps the whole-repository rule.
advantages: Needs only the ownership map the repository already keeps; an unrelated component's commit leaves the row current.
disadvantages: Keeps a result when a shared utility the arm imports is owned by another component, which the ownership map does not say.

name: Import closure
description: For a Python arm, the repository files its implementation module imports, transitively, found by reading the source (nothing is run), plus its evaluation folder; a changed file that is not Python, a non-Python arm or a computed import falls back to the component rule.
advantages: Follows what the code really imports, so a shared utility counts for the arms that use it and not for the others.
disadvantages: Cannot see what code reads at run time by a computed name or a data file outside the ownership map, so those fall back to the component rule.

name: Index folder in the user's home
description: A folder named by an environment variable, else a hidden folder in the home directory, holding one row per project and an index page generated from the rows between markers.
advantages: Found by name like the settings folder of other tools, works offline, keeps the person's own routing outside the generated part, and lists projects that live online. Selected because: it scores highest on the lookup cases, where both other arms miss projects the guidance never named.
disadvantages: One more place to keep current; only as complete as the person makes it.

name: Routing rows in the skill's index
description: Rows written into the skill's own index that say, for named projects, where to start and what they use.
advantages: Needs no setup for the author's own projects.
disadvantages: Names projects the public reader does not work on, goes stale when a project moves, and cannot know a project added later.

name: Each project's own records only
description: From a path, climb to the nearest configuration and read that project's own records.
advantages: No extra structure to keep.
disadvantages: Knows no other project, no file to read first and no relation between projects, and cannot list.

name: Declarations in code with one cascade
description: Code declares a solution (`@solution`) and its alternatives (`@implementation`, or `register` for another package's class); calling the interface runs the chosen one. One cascade decides, the innermost layer winning: per call, context, environment, deployment, then the project default, which is the solution's selected cell in the records. The selection table and its resolver remain the lower layer.
advantages: Declared once where the code is; a name swaps an implementation for one call, a block, a process or a deployment; no second copy of the default; an unknown name fails with the choices and the layer that named it. Selected because: built on the table it keeps; the same cases pin both layers, and the table alone fails the declared ones
disadvantages: Reads the records at run time, or a snapshot shipped with the package, and the interface function's own body is never run.

name: Selector class and table
description: The selector class in `esoi/select.py`: a pure-data table lists each solution's implementations and default, and a resolver turns a name, an override or the default into the class, importing it lazily.
advantages: No logic at the program's call sites, optional dependencies load only when chosen, and a typo fails with the choices.
disadvantages: Python only, and the embedding program must ship the table; kept as the lower layer under the declared one.

name: Dependency-ordered assembler
description: An Assembler over a package's solutions: it resolves each part by validated name through the cascade, builds the parts in dependency order and hands each typed need to the part that declares it.
advantages: Parts meet by name, so configuration, a row or an environment variable can swap an implementation; a cycle or an unmet need fails at startup naming the chain; nothing is imported that no record vouches for.
disadvantages: Strict by design: it ignores the deployment table, override() and the process environment and refuses dots and colons in names, and a part nothing can build fails at assembly (at first use for a Lazy part).
